judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the green 'INSCREVA-SE' button (text 'Inscreva-se', uppercased by CSS) in the 'alertas grátis do Poder360' subscribe box. It links to the Poder360 WhatsApp channel. Its text is the same as the Telegram button's, which goes to t.me/Poder360. The only thing that tells it apart is the icon in the sibling div just before it: a separate <a> to the same URL whose img has alt "WhatsApp" (visible as the WhatsApp logo). I tried that as the reason it passes, and it does not hold. The icon and the button are in separate sibling divs (separate blocks), and the shared parent is a generic div. That is not the same sentence, paragraph, list item or table cell. The link has no aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby or title (the snapshot's ax data shows only name INSCREVA-SE), and the fieldset legend 'Formulário de cadastro' / label 'alertas grátis do Poder360' does not name the channel. To learn the channel, a screen-reader user has to leave the link and read the previous one. WCAG's failure F63 names exactly this: 'If the user must leave the link to search for the context, the context is not programmatically determined link context'. Its first example is a 'Read More' link next to the content that explains it. H2 (combining adjacent image and text links) is only advisory for 2.4.4 and assumes the text link describes itself, which this one does not. The two links lead to different apps, so the channel is part of each link's purpose, and the purpose is not ambiguous to users in general. The message overstates the case ('nothing around this one'), since the logo sits right next to it visually and in the DOM. Read as a claim about programmatically determined link context, though, it is a real 2.4.4 failure. The live page (checked 2026-10-11) still has the same markup.
